chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a garment that is touched by saffron, then it is washed but the color does not disappear. He was asked: 'Is one prohibited from wearing it in Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it when its aroma disappears, and even if all of it was dyed, as long as it turns to whiteness and is washed, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانُ: Saffron, used here as a dye
key_terms.ضَرَبَ إِلَى الْبَيَاضِ: Turned to whiteness / lightened in color
key_terms.يُحْرَمُ: To be prohibited (specifically from wearing in Ihram)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim wear saffron-dyed clothes during Ihram if the color doesn't wash out completely?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition on wearing sewn garments or specific colors in Ihram is lifted if the distinguishing feature (scent or distinct color) is removed through washing. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the restriction targets the *appearance* of luxury or distinction rather than the material itself, allowing for practical flexibility in ritual purity and dress. The hadith further establishes that even fully dyed garments are permissible if they fade to a neutral white, emphasizing the importance of the garment's final state over its initial treatment.
